record.title: The DICTO Yantra: Unique and Traditional, Exact but Not Constructible
record.abstract: The DICTO Yantra is the only Śrī Yantra that meets Huet's conditions, Kulaichev's (b), (c) and (d), with (d) stated as the incircle of the bindu, the Cleo-Antonius product uv = 2/φ³ in place of (a), and admissibility, and it has the traditional form: 43 triangles, 18 marmas and 24 sandhis (Theorem 15 and Proposition 11). The proof is computer-assisted, a certified computation: exact divisor lemma and elimination over ℚ(√5), real roots certified by three isolators, ball arithmetic and the Krawczyk test; an independent second census agrees. Kulaichev's own conditions force exactly one figure too, and it is not the traditional yantra: Kulaichev's yantra is the only Śrī Yantra that meets Huet's conditions, Kulaichev's four conditions and admissibility, and it has 45 regions, 41 triangles and 4 four-sided, and 28 sandhis, not 43 triangles and 24 sandhis (Theorem 14, a computer-assisted proof of the same kind). Theorem 14's result is also proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib, by a separate, kernel-checked route, registered on Palomar as PALOMAR-2026-11-17-000006. This answers the uniqueness question Kulaichev asked in 1984. Both yantras are solved exactly: the great slopes of the DICTO Yantra on the Cleo-Antonius and of Kulaichev's classical yantra have minimal polynomials of degree 160 and 348 (Theorems 9 and 10).
